notice: Synthetic, hand-written test input. Not a mock of any canonical interface and never a production fallback. A pass against this fixture is fixture evidence only.

plantedDefect.cause: loop bound is readings.length - 1, so the final reading is never compared

input.encoding: utf-8, LF line endings, no NUL
rules: maxDepth counts path segments including the file name: src/tide.mjs has 2.
allowedPathPattern must match the whole relative path. Use a full-match call, or an engine in which $ cannot match before a trailing newline.

Paths are relative, use / as the separator, and are compared as bytes. Every segment starts with a letter or digit, so . and .. segments, hidden files, spaces and shell metacharacters are all outside the pattern.

taskPlusInput.why: Keeps the whole fixture inlinable in one task if no data-staging channel exists. Upstream maxTaskLength is 40000 characters at OpenCoven/coven-agents@3a4f3ff4130860d0abda1d2207b43b2f9d372180:packages/agent-contracts/contract-descriptor.ts:37. This bound is in bytes, which is never smaller than the character count, and it excludes any framing an inlining scheme adds; the margin to 40000 is left for that.

report.why: task.md asks for a report under 8000 bytes, so the largest acceptable report is 7999 bytes (RP-15). 16384 is the size above which a report must be refused or explicitly truncated, never silently accepted (RP-02); it is #5's proposal until #3 and #4 publish a bound.

artifacts.why: The only artifact a run produces is the report. The provenance #4 exports with it is derived from canonical records by the export, not written by the run. If #4 stores provenance as a second artifact, this bound changes with that contract.

runtime.why: Issue #1: 900 seconds or the tighter existing bound.

unresolved: How the input is staged into the sandbox as bounded data is #3's decision and an upstream gap (no data-staging channel at the pinned coven-agents revision). This fixture does not assume a mechanism.
How the input bytes are bound into the admission payload digest is #3's decision. This fixture publishes hashes; it does not define a digest contract.

If the input is inlined into the task text, the untrusted notice in notes/automation-notice.txt sits inside the instruction channel rather than beside it. That makes the injection case harder and is a reason to prefer a data-staging channel; it is #3's decision.
